resources.string: The published contract: what a plugin may declare, and what was accepted or refused here.

A declared capability is either a read or a proposal. There is deliberately no capability that writes hardware: every write in this app goes through the arbiter, and a plugin that could write directly would remove the guard built to stop two owners writing the same knob.
This text is what the parser reads. It cannot drift from the code, because it is generated from it.
Listing the manifest folder with root, then evaluating each manifest against the contract.
Reported by the plugin, not measured by us
The manifest folder holds no plugin folders. Nothing is wrong: this is the default state of the feature.
Manifest folder does not exist yet
%1$s has not been created on this device, so there is nothing to read. Creating it is all a plugin author needs to do.
The folder exists at %1$s but the shell could not read it. Root is required to list it.
The id is not usable as a folder name. Use lowercase Latin letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, and never two dots in a row.
The version must start with digits, for example 1.0.0.
The declared API level is missing or below 1.
The declared API level is newer than this build understands, so it is not run at all.
The kind is not one of the published kinds.
The capability is not part of this contract. An unknown capability is refused rather than ignored, so nothing runs with fewer rights than it asked for.
A plugin must declare at least one capability.
Another plugin with this id was already accepted, so this one is not used.

Without a published contract, anyone extending this app has to guess the shape of our internal files, and we cannot tell a valid extension from a broken one. With it, the limit is stated: a plugin declares intent and reads; it never writes hardware, and every refusal above names the exact field that failed.
